title: Incremental telemetry viz schema (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
- Sketch an incremental (streaming-friendly) telemetry payload shape optimized for UI-side progressive rendering and low-cardinality aggregation. Goal is to let dashboards render rough results quickly and refine as more deltas arrive, while keeping payloads bounded for mobile/web clients.

High level idea (notes to self):
- Emit compact events (base + delta) keyed by series_id (tenant+route+model+metric).
- Each message includes a sequence window [t_start, t_end] and a small summary bucket (count, sum, min, max) + optional sketches (p95 sketch ref) when available.
- Clients keep a lightweight in-memory state per series and can apply idempotent merges using a monotonic seq or vector clock.

Wire shape (compact JSON-y pseudo):
- top-level envelope: { version, tenant_id, batch_id, partial: true|false, items: [...] }
- item: { series_id, seq_id, t_window_start, t_window_end, baseline?: bool, summary: {n, sum, min, max}, histogram_id?: shortRef, sketch?: base64, tags?: [k=v,...] }

Example message (one line):
{"version":"0.2","tenant_id":"acme","batch_id":"b-2026-02-25-001","partial":true,"items":[{"series_id":"acme|r:generate|m:gpt-7|c:latency","seq_id":2382,"t_window_start":1700000000,"t_window_end":1700000060,"summary":{"n":12,"sum":972.3,"min":60.2,"max":150.7},"tags":["region:us-west","route:chat"]}]}

Merge semantics (informal):
- seq_id is monotonic per series. Clients track last_applied_seq per series. If incoming.seq_id <= last -> drop. If > last, merge summary additive. If partial windows overlap, prefer baseline records (baseline=true) as ground truth and treat overlapping partials as estimations.
- For out-of-order messages we include batch_id + origin_ts to allow client to request re-fetch for gaps (TODO: lightweight gap query API).

Visualization usage patterns:
- Progressive line charts: render aggregated summary.sum / summary.n as average; show shaded band from min/max; update as new items arrive.
- Sparklines / micro charts: keep last N windows; each window is small (<= 64 bytes per item typical).
- Heatmaps: produce sparse tile updates keyed by time_bucket + series_hash to reduce cardinality.

Compression & transport notes:
- Use newline-delimited JSON for streaming (HTTP/2 or websocket). Recommend gzip for batches; consider binary protobuf for mobile clients if we need tighter budgets.
- Provide a compressed sketch proto for p95/p99 (e.g., t-digest base64) when clients request higher fidelity.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent derived metrics (cost_per_token) without exploding series cardinality? Option: emit base metrics and let UI compute derived via formula from metadata.
- Retention model for client-side state: evict if no updates for 24h? 1h? Need SRE input.
- Should we include semantic tags as separate map vs flattened list of strings? Flattened is smaller but harder to query.
- Backfill API: lightweight endpoint to request baseline snapshot for a set of series_ids + time range. Minimal surface: POST /v1/telemetry/snapshot { tenant, series_ids[], t_start, t_end } -> full-baseline batch.

Minimal server-side API sketch:
POST /v1/telemetry/ingest (internal) -> accepts envelope; returns 202 + ack_id.
GET /v1/telemetry/stream?tenant=acme&since_ack=xxx -> SSE/WS stream of envelopes.
POST /v1/telemetry/snapshot -> returns baseline snapshot JSON (for client rehydration).

Local UX mock (how dashboard consumes):
1) open dashboard -> call snapshot for top N series -> render baseline chart.
2) open websocket to stream incremental envelopes -> apply incoming partials to charts (shaded delta).
3) on detect gap (seq jumps) -> request snapshot for that gap.

Small ascii diagram:
[server ingest] -> [event store (compact batches)] -> [stream router] -> [ws/sse sink] -> [client dashboard state] -> render
                                ^                                                  |
                                |                                                  v
                            [snapshot API] --------------------------------> [client rehydrate]

Notes to self: keep shape versioned (version field) so we can iterate. Try to prototype on top of current obs pipeline (Luca said we can piggyback on kafka topic obs-stream-compact). Start with v0.1 baseline-only then v0.2 add sketches.

Next steps:
- Prototype schema serializer (JS) + lightweight client merger (5 files).
- Spike compression tradeoffs (ndjson gzip vs protobuf).
- Discuss retention/eviction with SRE and product dashboards team.
- Wire up a tiny demo dashboard (storybook) showing progressive updates.

Random TODOs (sticky):
- Add deterministic series_id algorithm (hash order of tags) and document collision risk.
- Decide if we allow multi-tenant stream connectors or per-tenant topics.
- Add example of histogram sketch encoding (t-digest base64)

References / links in head: OBS-telemetry-v1, jira OBS-1234, github PR 42 for serializer.

~Maya
